chunks.arabic_text: عَلِيّ بْن الْعَبَّاس، الْجَرَذِينِيّ، أَبُو الْحَسَن، الرَّازِيّ.

translations.en: Ali ibn al-Abbas, al-Jaradhinī, Abū al-Ḥasan, al-Rāzī.

chunks.arabic_text: مَشْهُورٌور. لَهُ تَصْنِيف فِي الْمَمْدُوحِينَ وَالْمَذْمُومِينَ يَدُلّ عَلَى خَبْثِهِ وَتَهَالُك مَذْهَبِهِ. لَا يُلْتَفَت إِلَيْهِ، وَلَا يُعْبَأ بِمَا رَوَاهُ.

translations.en: Famous. He has a compilation about the praised and the censured that indicates his filth and the languor of his madhhab. He is not turned to, and what he narrates is insignificant.

en.summary: Al-Ghadā'irī characterizes ʿAlī ibn al-ʿAbbās al-Jarādhīnī al-Rāzī as a prominent but flawed narrator, noting that his work *Al-Mamdūḥīn wa al-Madhūmīn* reveals his doctrinal depth (or perhaps 'filth' depending on the reading of *khabath*) and the lethargy of his school. Despite being 'famous,' he is largely disregarded in hadith criticism, with his narrations considered insignificant due to his specific theological or scholarly disposition.
en.seo_question: Who is Ali ibn al-Abbas al-Jaradhinī and what is his status in Shia hadith sciences?

key_terms.مَشْهُور: Famous (a specific grade in rijal indicating a narrator is well-known but not necessarily highly reliable)
key_terms.الْمَمْدُوحِينَ وَالْمَذْمُومِينَ: The Praised and the Censured (title of his work)
key_terms.خَبْث: Filth/Depth (often used in rijal to denote a specific quality, sometimes positive depth, sometimes negative corruption depending on context; here linked to languor)
